sources.name: Acquire.com
sources.notes: Companies and modules for sale. Listings are visible only to signed-in buyers, so this needs stored credentials — which the system deliberately does not hold yet, and which is a decision to take on purpose rather than by default. Note the direction: an acquisition SPENDS money, so it is never added into a funding total.

sources.name: Abu Dhabi Investment Office — incentive programmes
sources.notes: Innovation and investment incentives for companies establishing in Abu Dhabi. Relevant through Oolala Next FZ-LLC — the entity route matters here more than the call itself.

sources.name: Aides-territoires
sources.notes: Aggregates French aid for local authorities and associations, including REGIONAL schemes. The most direct answer to 'aid is under-represented'. Relevant above all to Les Vieilles Pierres and Maisons.co.

sources.name: BOAMP — Bulletin officiel des annonces de marchés publics
sources.notes: French public procurement INCLUDING below the European thresholds — the band where a studio this size actually wins. The highest-value source not yet connected. An open-data API is understood to exist; its shape has not been verified from this environment.

sources.name: Bpifrance
sources.notes: Grants, repayable advances, guarantees and equity. Covers three of the kinds the taxonomy now distinguishes, which is why they were worth distinguishing.

sources.name: Research and innovation tax credits (CIR, CII, JEI)
sources.notes: Not a call site and never will be: a fiscal status claimed on a filing. It is listed because the taxonomy can now represent it — before TAX_INCENTIVE existed, a tax credit could not pass the gate at any evidence level.

sources.name: EU Funding & Tenders portal (SEDIA)
sources.notes: Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, Creative Europe, EIC. The connector exists and is exercised against a recorded response only — it has never completed a live run. Status stays FIXTURE_ONLY until one does.

sources.name: Flippa
sources.notes: Digital assets and small software businesses. Public listings; no connector.

sources.name: France 2030 / ADEME calls
sources.notes: National programme calls. Typically large consortia — relevant to BAWABA rather than to the smaller ventures.

sources.name: Hub71
sources.notes: Abu Dhabi tech ecosystem: incentive packages and cohorts. One Hub71 record already sits in the dataset from the Milestone-0 seed, entered by hand — this entry makes that source explicit rather than incidental.

sources.name: Malt, Comet and French consulting marketplaces
sources.notes: Visible only to signed-in members, which makes scraping both a terms question and a credentials question. Manual intake until there is a reason to resolve both.

sources.name: Région Bretagne — aides et appels à projets
sources.notes: Regional aid for Brittany: heritage, culture, tourism, digital, business development. Explicitly requested. No machine access identified — watched by hand, and anything found goes through the manual intake so it lands in the same ledger with the same verification.

sources.name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily
sources.notes: Above-EU-threshold public procurement. A real run retrieved from it and the response is the repository's test fixture. Covers only contracts ABOVE the European thresholds — the ones a studio of this size wins are usually below, which is why BOAMP matters more.

sources.name: UAE federal and emirate procurement portals
sources.notes: Each emirate and several federal entities run their own portal, most requiring supplier registration. No single machine-readable index is known to exist. Treated as manual watch rather than pretending a connector is coming.

sources.name: Find a Tender (UK)
sources.notes: The UK's post-Brexit equivalent of TED. Publishes an OCDS feed, which would make it the second-easiest connector after TED.

sources.name: UN Global Marketplace
sources.notes: UN agency procurement. One UNESCO record in the dataset came from here, entered by hand. Registration required to bid; the notices themselves are public.

sources.name: Upwork
sources.notes: Clients posting paid software work. An API exists behind OAuth, and the terms of service govern what may be automated — so this is BLOCKED rather than DECLARED until that is read properly. Postings found by hand go through the manual intake today.

sources.name: Development bank procurement (World Bank, AfDB, EBRD)
sources.notes: Sport, leisure and social infrastructure in emerging markets — the realistic route for padel.design and District 267, neither of which any European source covers.
